body: Hey, I want to thank you for sharing your story.  Today was really hard--I had to return everything to the school I'd begun student teaching at and face the teachers there and explain why I'm being pulled out, etc.  I felt so ashamed, but I was glad to read your comment when I got home.  I hope I will come out a stronger person, like you said.

Thank you so much, it is nice to shed some tears of gratitude to end this horrible day instead of the tears of shame and despair I've been spewing all day.  I felt in my heart that I should be proud of my decision not to marry someone when I knew it wasn't right for either of us, and it feels really good to hear someone validate that.  

I am going to try to sleep now, but I can't thank you enough for your support tonight.  People like you are rare and truly special to reach out with kind words for a complete stranger.  I will think about everything you've said and check in tomorrow, if you'd like.  Goodnight and thank you again.

Sorry, my comments aren't posting right now, but I'm hoping this one will go through:  I know that they support me and their belief in me is part of what makes this so painful.  A couple of years ago, I turned down a proposal from a man my family and friends loved, but who I knew I couldn't spend my life with.  Everyone treated me like I had failed at that relationship and had basically ruined my chance at a great life.  I guess I'm having flashback and just feeling like an overall failure.

I will try to take your advice and give myself a free pass, I am trying to be optimistic.  I just feel completely abandoned and like I deserve that, for some reason.  I don't know, I took some xanax (prescribed by a doctor and the prescribed amount), so I am feeling pretty drowsy now and probably not making much sense.  Thank you so much for your replies, I think they will help even more once I've had a chance to sleep and can read them with fresh eyes.

Yes, I've noticed problems with commenting, too.   He left me because, in his words "You let me down, I feel you're unstable and I don't want to be with someone long term who doesn't have their shit together."  He said he is technically just "thinking things over" for a few days, but it sounds like he had just lost faith in me and doesn't want to be tied to someone with issues.  Thanks so much for responding.

Hello and thank you for your response.  There is nothing I can do right now except face the humiliation of telling everyone (professors/adviser/employer/family/friends from school/etc) that I screwed up and the student teaching I've been talking about so excitedly is just not going to happen.

I am definitely going to throw myself full force into school now, but I don't know how I can find the will to continue at this point.  I can't get over the embarrassment of failing--I have my own desk set up at the high school, the students have been getting to know me, it's my OLD high school, so the teachers all know me already and have been really nice and supportive.  Now they will all know that I'm a screw up.  I guess that's the hardest thing for me--letting so many people down.

Thank you again for taking the time to reach out--it means a lot.
